161	### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR
162	
163	**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
164	not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
165	against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
166	AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
167	work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
168	wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
169	there.
170	
171	**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
172	`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
173	`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
174	already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
175	the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
176	general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
177	branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
178	`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
179	**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
180	plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
181	before touching it.
182	
183	**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
184	confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
185	`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
186	grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.
187	
188	**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
189	fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
190	hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
191	Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
192	notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.
193	
194	**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
195	as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
196	new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
197	.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
198	if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
199	mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
200	open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
201	how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
202	nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.
203	
204	### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)
205	
206	**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
207	Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
208	the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
209	ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
210	actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
211	(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
212	only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
213	swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
214	intended to survive that swap unchanged.
215	
216	**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
217	both interim, only one of which changes later:
218	1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
219	   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
220	   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
221	2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
222	   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
223	   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
224	   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
225	   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
226	   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
227	   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.
228	
229	**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
230	- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
231	  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
232	  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
233	  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
234	  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
235	- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
236	  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
237	  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
238	  change; only where the input object comes from does.
239	- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
240	  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
241	  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
242	  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
243	- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
244	  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
245	  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
246	  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
247	  mapper already planned.
248	
249	**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
250	- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
251	  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
252	- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
253	  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by

### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR

**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
there.

**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
before touching it.

**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.

**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.

**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
intended to survive that swap unchanged.

**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
both interim, only one of which changes later:
1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.

**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
  change; only where the input object comes from does.
- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
  mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.
- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather
  than creating a duplicate entry — required for AC 2's "most-recent-first" to hold up under repeat
  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).
- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08, then SUPERSEDED same day once the 24-ID fetch limit
  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =
  500` was set as a generous engineering safety ceiling against unbounded growth. **That reasoning
  is now incomplete, not wrong** — it was correct given what was known at the time, but didn't yet
  account for two facts discovered later the same day: (1) Shopper Products `getProducts` has a
  hard 24-ID-per-request limit (SDK's own doc comment, independently confirmed twice during Phase 1
  implementation), and (2) Marcel decided the Full History page caps its fetch/display at 24 rather
  than batching (see B2 below). Given Full History will **never** show more than 24 items and the
  rail never shows more than 5, storing more than 24 serves no purpose — nothing beyond item 24 is
  reachable from any UI this build has. **`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24`, superseding
  the `500` above.** This was caught by Phase 1's own implementer, who read this plan directly,
  found the contradiction between what it was told to build and what this section said, and
  correctly surfaced it rather than silently picking a side — exactly the discipline this plan
  asks for elsewhere. **Open Question 17 is re-closed at the new number** — no further confirmation
  needed; this is a direct, logical consequence of Marcel's own 24-cap decision, not a new
  independent judgement call.

**What stays exactly as planned, unaffected by this whole section:** A2 (variation config), A5 (rail
UI), B1 (grid UI) — all purely presentational, receive cards as props, and have never cared where
those props came from. This is the container/presentational split (`components.md`) paying off
exactly as designed.

**To verify at implementation time, not guessed here:** the exact `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
hook name for a batch product-detail fetch (likely `useProducts`, plural, alongside the already-used
singular `useProduct` — confirm against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` per AGENTS.md's
own Gotchas note before trusting the name).

**Not a scope decision for this PR:** what the Einstein follow-up ticket looks like in detail (does
it reuse the `getProducts`-and-map layer, or fully replace it with `fetchRecProductDetails`'s own
internal enrichment?). Left for that ticket, once it exists — this section only needs to ship a
clean, honest interim, not pre-solve the migration.

## PostBuild Conformance Report — SFCC-83/84 Recently Viewed

### Critical setup correction (must be stated up front)

Local `develop` was **6 days stale** (`a18c68b`, 2026-09-04) versus `origin/develop` (`3cec638`, 2026-09-10 — today). `git merge-base develop HEAD` against the stale local ref pulled in ~250 files of already-merged, unrelated work (SFCC-236 product-card family, SFCC-731 gallery, SFCC-742 wishlist drawer, SFCC-737, CI workflow files, `config/*.js`, `vitest.config.ts`) that had already landed on `origin/develop` via PRs #85/#86/#81/#83/#103/#104/#89/#99/#101/#92/#91/#87/#88/#84/#105 before this branch's own SFCC-83/84 work began. After `git fetch origin develop`, `git merge-base origin/develop HEAD` resolves to `3cec638` — the true tip of `develop` — and isolates exactly the branch's own 27 SFCC-83/84 commits (`f5928db`...`38b8601`). All analysis below uses this corrected base. The working tree is clean (the session's git-status snapshot showing "M" files was itself stale — everything is committed).

---

### 1. Manifest vs. real diff — file lists

**Plan manifest** (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md`, §3 "File manifest," lines 298–350): **27 unique files**. All 27 were touched — **zero under-delivery at the file level**.

**Real diff** (`git diff 3cec638..HEAD --numstat`, excluding `.claude/registry/*.md`): **39 files**. Of these, **27 match the manifest exactly**; **12 do not**.

Registry churn (auto-generated, not a finding, per instructions): `.claude/registry/components.md`, `hooks.md`, `pages.md`, `routes.md`, `utils.md`. No compiled-translation files appear in the corrected diff at all.

### 2. Scope findings — diff files not in the manifest

**Major (8 files) — genuine, documented scope creep, not a technicality:**

All 8 land in a single commit lineage: `d752252` (`fix(product-list): resolve colour-blind images and complete card interactions`, Sep 9 10:52) plus its test-fixup follow-on `21d5807`, and a second, unrelated commit `dd72b62`.

| File | Tier/Owner | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` | Untiered-by-canon, CODEOWNERS: `overrides/app/pages/product-list/` → `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` | Wires `getPriceData` was/now pricing, `resolveOrderableVariant` for real Add-to-Bag, `availability`/`represented_products` search fields into PLP's **main grid** card mapper |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts` | same | Test coverage for the above (302/15 lines) |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` | Tier 3-by-plan-convention, CODEOWNERS:176 `ui-kits/` → squad-a+b | Adds `primaryImageFallbacks` cascade, removes `!gallery` gate so hover-swap runs during gallery mode |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` | same | Test coverage for the above (110/3 lines) |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` | same | Changes `showNotifyMeButton` gating — Notify Me now ships visible-but-inert |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.test.tsx` | same | Test coverage for the above |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts` | same, from commit `dd72b62` | Fixed gap to 8px instead of `space-between` — a PDP size-selector styling fix with no stated connection to Recently Viewed (whose own `recentlyViewed` variation explicitly ships `showSizeChips: false`, per A2) |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts` | same | Test coverage for the above |

This isn't a borderline call — **the plan explicitly documents deciding not to do this**. Plan.md line 1316–1319 (Open Question 16, closed 2026-09-08, the day before `d752252` was committed):

> "**Not done:** actually wiring `getPriceData` into `productListCardMapper.ts`'s runtime behaviour... that changes already-shipped PLP behaviour on a file outside this branch's own scope, a bigger, separate call than 'fix the inaccurate comment.' Left as a genuine fast-follow if wanted, not assumed."

`d752252`'s own commit message does exactly the thing the plan ruled out one day earlier: *"was/now pricing is wired through getPriceData... Add to Bag now resolves the actually-selected size's real variant... Notify Me ships visible-but-inert."* It also violates A2's own explicit, named pass criterion (plan.md line 466–467): *"Confined entirely to `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or `ZimmProductCardMedia`, matching this step's existing file manifest exactly."* `productListCardMapper.ts`/`.test.ts` are not mentioned anywhere in the manifest at all.

**Minor (4 files) — manifest omissions, not real creep:**

| File | Note |
|---|---|
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.test.ts` | Companion test for the manifested `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` (CREATE) |
| `.../pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` | Companion test for the manifested `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (CREATE) |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` | Not a manifest row, but implements the exact `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS` per-breakpoint mechanism B3 explicitly designs (plan.md line 1075) — extracted to a hook rather than left inline |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.test.ts` | Test for the above |

Not flagged as scope creep — traceable directly to planned decisions, just not itemized as separate manifest rows.

**Within an in-manifest file:** `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` is in the manifest, but only for "add one `RecommendedProducts` call site." The actual diff (95/18 lines, mostly from `d752252`) also carries part of the PLP-card-completion rework described above — over-delivery inside a nominally-planned file.

### 3. Tier mismatches

- **Terminology, not a governance error.** The manifest's "Tier 3"/"Untiered" labels don't exist in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` or `protectedFiles.md`, which define only Tier 1 and Tier 2. Spot-checked every manifest row that claims Tier 1/Tier 2 status against those two files (`theme/components/index.ts` → Tier 2 ✓ matches protectedFiles.md; `routes.tsx` → Tier 2 Global Shell ✓ matches; `recommended-products/` → Tier 2 ✓ matches) — none understate real protection. "Tier 3" is the plan's own finer CODEOWNERS-derived label for squad ownership beyond the two canonical tiers; harmless but worth flagging since it's not this repo's actual taxonomy.
- **Real mismatch: `product-list/` ownership.** The manifest labels `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` "Tier 3 (Squad A page)," owner `pwa-squad-a`, citing `.claude/rules/squadA.md`. `squadA.md` (a self-described **draft**) does list `overrides/app/pages/product-list/**` as Squad A territory. But the live `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS` (line 163) routes `overrides/app/pages/product-list/` to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` — the opposite squad. This is a pre-existing conflict between two of this repo's own docs (not introduced by this build), but it means the plan's "notify Squad A Lead" premise doesn't match the file that will actually gate the PR merge.
- No Tier 1 file appears anywhere in the diff. Confirmed against `frozenFiles.md`'s full list (`theme/foundation/`, `config/`, `ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js`, `.github/workflows/`, hooks list, etc.) — none touched.

### 4. Step-breakdown vs. real commit history — sanity check

A1→A6 map cleanly, one commit each: `f5928db`(A1)→`a1279fe`(A2)→`b5f4a45`(A3)→`6fb1e5c`(A4)→`ab26ee6`(A5)→`e0f9991`(A6). Consistent with the plan's "one commit per step" rule (line 354).

That discipline breaks down at `f897773`, a large WIP checkpoint whose own message states: *"Exists solely as a safe restore point before a temporary local merge of PR #81... Real commit history for this work will be organized separately later."* It bundles B1 (Grid CREATE), B2 (page/route CREATE), the `useRecentlyViewedGate`→`useRecentlyViewedHistory` rename, and a first touch of `productListCardMapper.ts`, all in one 33-file commit — never subsequently reorganized into per-step commits as the message anticipated. The remaining 19 commits are testing-driven fixes (breakpoint thresholds, grid gaps/padding, Cart exclusion, bleed margins, colour-blind images) that don't map to discrete plan steps at all — expected for work built through direct conversational iteration rather than the structured loop, and not itself a scope problem. `d752252` and `dd72b62` (the two commits behind the 8 major/minor scope findings above) sit inside that same unstructured tail.

---

## Verdict

**OVER** — Every named manifest item was delivered (no under-delivery). But the diff also contains 8 files the plan never named, in a domain the plan's own text explicitly closed off the day before it was written: `productListCardMapper.ts`/`.test.ts` (PLP main-grid pricing/Add-to-Bag/Notify-Me rework — plan.md line 1316–1319 says plainly "not done... outside this branch's own scope"), `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`+test and `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`+test (directly contradicting A2's own pass criterion, plan.md line 466–467: "no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or `ZimmProductCardMedia`"), and `zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts`+test (an unrelated PDP size-chip fix with no stated tie to Recently Viewed, whose own variation disables size chips entirely). All 8 trace to two commits: `d752252` and `dd72b62`. Separately, 4 files (2 companion test files, 1 new hook + its test implementing an already-designed B3 mechanism) are manifest omissions rather than real creep, and the `product-list/` squadA.md-vs-CODEOWNERS ownership conflict is a pre-existing doc drift worth surfacing but not blocking. No Tier 1 file was touched.
